Stephen Vincent Benét, John Brown’s Body.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/stephen-vincent-benet/john-browns-body

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Stephen Vincent Benét, the author, died 1943.

First publication of the text used: 1928 (SE colophon: 'John Brown’s Body was published in 1928 by Stephen Vincent Benét.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the rights statement quoted below places the text in the United States public domain. The text was first published in 1928, before 1931.
- Country of origin: the last person to die among those named above died in 1943 (Stephen Vincent Benét). The text is public domain in each country that could be its country of first publication, because each of these has a term of life + 70 years or less: United Kingdom, Ireland, United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. For a life + 70 years term, the text entered the public domain on 1 January 2014. No fact points to France, Spain, Mexico, Colombia or Russia/USSR as a country of first publication.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
